newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Nomura directors involved in scandal resign.
newsitem.headline: Two Nomura directors involved in scandal resign.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said two company executives involved in an irregular dealings scandal resigned as managing directors as of Monday.
Nomura said in a statement that the company had accepted the resignations of the two managing directors, whom it named as Shimpei Matsuki and Nobutaka Fujikura.
A Nomura spokesman said that they were the two directors who had been involved in dubious deals that Nomura admitted last week appear to have broken the law.
Asked whether any more Nomura officials would resign, such as Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki, the spokesman said he had not heard of any more resignation plans.
Japanese media reported last week that the Nomura president has offered to step down once the investigation into the transactions had been completed.

Last Thursday, Nomura said the two directors apparently made discretionary transactions and moved profits raised from Nomura's own funds to a corporate customer's account, actions which are against the law.

Nomura at that time could not confirm reports the corporate client was run by a relative of a "sokaiya" racketeer, but said that the client had a longstanding relationship with the directors and family ties to a Nomura shareholder.
Sokaiya, often linked to Japan's "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices.
